newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S NFI PROGRESS TO INJECT $10 MLN IN 3 FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S NFI PROGRESS TO INJECT $10 MLN IN 3 FIRMS.

text.p: Poland's National Investment Fund Progress SA (NFI no.4) plans to increase the capital of three firms from its portfolio by a total of $10 million, the president of the fund said on Monday.
"Within a dozen or so weeks we want to increase the share capital in three of our companies -- Tymbark SA, FMG Fameg SA and Zelmot," Jaroslaw Dabrowski told a news conference.
"The fund will invest about $10 million in those companies, this is a part of the fund's liquid assets which now total $28 million," Dabrowski told Reuters after the conference.
He said the funds would be used to expand production capacity of fruit and vegetable processor Tymbark, furniture maker Fameg and manufacturer of automotive lighting accessories Zelmot.
Dabrowski said that Progress was considering investments in about 10 companies outside its portfolio and expected to conclude three of them this year.
"Within the next few weeks we should conclude one of them in an area which is not represented in the NFI programme -- retailing and distribution," he said.
Dabrowski added that this year the fund planned to float on the Warsaw bourse only a maker of power cables for electric trains, Przedsiebiorstwo Kolejowych Robot Elektryfikacyjnych.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equity stakes in the remaining firms.
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been entitled to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
